title: Shut off a pre-rinse spray valve left locked on over a dish sink
instruction: The pre-rinse sprayer has been left on. Turn it off and leave it hanging over the sink.
context: Cleaning equipment and dishes is regular work for food preparation workers (908,500 US jobs in 2025, BLS). A commercial pre-rinse valve can be left running when its hold-down ring catches the squeeze handle. Recovery requires unloading the spring-loaded handle and disengaging its ring while controlling a hose-suspended head.
setup: Fixed layout, metres: x forward from the arm bases, y left, heights above the 0.7475 m station tabletop. Stainless dish table spans x 0.08–0.64, y -0.42–0.42; deck height 0.125. Its open sink spans x 0.14–0.52, y -0.23–0.23, floor height 0.003; backsplash is 0.015 thick and 0.25 above the deck. Fixed chrome faucet and riser stand at x 0.60, with an overhead support spring. A 0.50 m long, 0.019 m diameter rubber hose hangs from (0.33,0,0.885); its two equal sections each weigh 0.07 kg. The chrome valve hangs nozzle-down, spray face at (0.33,0,0.225), 0.10 above the deck. It is 0.160 long, body diameter 0.026 and nozzle diameter 0.034, mass 0.40 kg. On its left side is a 0.100 x 0.016 x 0.008 squeeze handle, mass 0.040 kg, spring-loaded toward off. A steel ring of 0.0015 wire radius holds its tip 0.008 from the body; ring travel is 0.0165, mass 0.015 kg, with a 0.014 x 0.019 x 0.0025 thumb tab. The locked valve initially sprays downward and swings gently (initial hinge velocity 0.20 rad/s). The stream represents hot rinse water; the faucet controls are fixed out of reach. On the deck: green foam sponge 0.071 x 0.091 x 0.027, 0.02 kg at (0.25,-0.33), yaw 0.3 rad; blue plastic plate 0.172 x 0.177 x 0.026, 0.12 kg at (0.46,0.32); ceramic mug 0.114 x 0.090 x 0.080, 0.30 kg at (0.47,-0.31), yaw 2.4 rad. All three are NVIDIA SimReady props.
scoring: Score is permanently 0 if, while water is flowing, its centreline crosses the deck-height plane outside the open basin, points level/upward above that plane, exits upward through the basin opening, or a sampled gripper point enters the spray cone (0–0.25 m below the nozzle, radius 0.015 + 0.15 times axial distance). Otherwise score 0 unless the ring has moved at least 0.008 m down, the handle is within 1 degree of its off stop, every sampled gripper point is at least 0.03 m from the valve and lower hose, and nozzle speed has remained below 0.03 m/s for 2 seconds. With these conditions, score 0.4. Score 1.0 when the nozzle is also within 0.08 m of its initial hanging point and all full-score conditions have held together for 3 seconds. Flow is on until the handle is within 2.5 degrees of its off stop. Evaluate at 20 Hz; the highest conditions satisfied at the last step determine the score, except the permanent spray violations. Physical checks use visible flow, a ruler and video.
reset_notes: Reset the joint positions and velocities, re-hook the ring with the handle squeezed, restore all props, and initialize the gentle swing. History resets only on episode reset. For a physical analogue use cold water with the same no-contact spray criterion; no hot water is needed.
fidelity: Custom articulated valve, handle, ring and sink; SimReady loose props. Spring handle and sliding ring use contact-driven joints; position-dependent joint stops approximate ring/handle engagement. Hose bending is a damped two-link pendulum. Water is a visible cone with geometric exposure checks, not fluid or heat simulation. Faucet and hose anchor are fixed. Dimensions are representative; spring/friction values are engineering approximations, not measurements of a specific product.
